status: DRAFT — pending reviewer sign-off. NO LINE SHIPS UNREVIEWED. Every line makes a factual claim about learners or about Japanese; the reviewer must be able to stand behind each one, or it is deleted, not softened.
firing_rules: Flourish only. At most one earned line per flourish; if a point announcement, capability line, and earned line all qualify, the earned line wins (rarest).
Each line fires ONCE per learner, ever. The trigger must actually have happened — a difficulty line fires on demonstrated correct use, not on finishing the reading.
Never model-generated, never paraphrased at runtime. Text ships exactly as reviewed.
The 'many quit before X' register was considered and DROPPED (Session 11): unverifiable and it primes quitting. Do not reintroduce it via synonyms ('most give up', 'few make it').

lines.trigger: correct contrastive/subject use of は vs が in practice
lines.text: は and が trouble learners for years — and you just used them correctly, unprompted.

lines.trigger: correct particle choice with a potential verb
lines.text: Particle choice with potential verbs is a place even advanced learners hesitate. You didn't.

lines.trigger: correct choice among たら/ば/と/なら in practice
lines.text: Japanese has four ways to say 'if', and picking the right one is famously hard. That was the right one.

lines.trigger: correct state (not progressive) reading of 〜ている
lines.text: 〜ている as a state rather than an action trips up almost everyone at first. You read it the way a native does.

lines.trigger: learner produces a natural sentence with omitted subject/topic
lines.text: Leaving the subject out — and being understood — is where Japanese stops feeling like translated English. That sentence did it.

lines.trigger: first kana lesson where every character was traced by hand
lines.text: You are writing these by hand. Plenty of learners never do — recognition fades; a hand that has drawn the strokes doesn't forget as easily.
Producing your own sentence is a different skill from picking the right answer — and it's one a test-prep syllabus rarely asks for.
Hearing a word and writing it with nothing to copy from — that is dictation, and it builds a kind of memory reading alone can't.
You are learning these sounds from a voice, not a chart. Your ear is training alongside your hand.

lines.trigger: learner can write their own name's katakana (all chars traced)
lines.text: You can write your name the way Japan will write it. Most visitors never can.

lines.trigger: capability threshold: menu-word set fully readable
lines.text: You could read this off a menu now — no pictures needed.

lines.trigger: correct use of a structure with no clean English equivalent (e.g. 〜てくれる)
lines.text: There's no neat English for what you just said — the gratitude is built into the grammar. Plenty of Japanese speakers struggle to carry that into English. You can now carry it the other way.

lines.trigger: smalltalk capability unit ~75% of prerequisite points cleared
lines.text: You're most of the way to holding small talk — greetings, weather, where you're from, what you do.
You can introduce yourself entirely in Japanese now. That's not a lesson — that's a thing you can do.
Every kana in the language is now yours to write. From here, everything you learn is words and ideas — the alphabet part of Japanese is behind you.

wiring_note: Triggers are named by construction/capability, not by lesson id — the grammar module's point ids drift with curriculum order, and the pain-point resurfacing map (curriculum-revisit-map-v1.md) is the right source for where these constructions are actually demonstrated. Wiring ships with Phase 1 flourish work; this file exists so the reviewer can pass judgment on the CLAIMS now.
